name: LA-02
label: Safe D

key_factors: Deep-blue district with D+25 partisan lean
Incumbent Troy Carter running with $1.4M raised
Republican challenger Peter Williams has shown no fundraising
Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~96%
model.rationale: Carter holds a heavily Democratic New Orleans-based seat, out-raised his little-known challenger by a wide margin, and markets price this as a near-certain Democratic hold. No polls or expert ratings exist, but fundamentals leave little doubt.
model.watch: Only a major scandal or unexpected incumbent retirement-level shock would put this in play.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Troy Carter seeks another term in a New Orleans-area district that leans Democratic by about 25 points. He enters the general election with roughly $1.4 million raised and a large cash advantage, while Republican Peter Williams has reported no fundraising and Libertarian and independent candidates also appear on the ballot. No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, but prediction markets give Carter about a 96 percent chance of winning.

The seat's fundamentals, the incumbent's financial edge, and the absence of any serious challenger infrastructure all point the same direction. Barring an unforeseen development, this race is expected to remain safely in Democratic hands.
